main_body: Flat-roofed desert house: a sand-coloured terrace roof seen from above (parapet, rug, hatch) over a plastered front wall with an arched door and a barred window
top_band: Rows 1-31 at x=32 are a sand roof surface (L~175, with a lighter L=202 parapet and edge highlight rows) under a dark outline at row 0. A distinct edge line at rows 28-31 is followed by a dark eave row at 32-33, then the front wall (L~122) from row 34.
evidence: The column scan shows a large light roof plane (L~175) separated from the darker front wall (L~122) by a lighter edge line at rows 28-31 and a dark shadow row at 32-33. The roof is a horizontal surface with parapet, rug and hatch, and below it is a south wall with a door and window. The door and window are inset with a frame and sill. The roof is barely foreshortened, but it clearly reads as a top surface above a front face, so both parts satisfy the contract.

style.evidence: The measured facts are well below both references. The candidate has 27 distinct colours against 66 and 185, and a median of 8 colours per tile against 11 and 18. Its flat-fill coverage is 15% against 0% for both references. The outlines are tinted brown (0% neutral), which is fine. The rug, the door and the wall bands are large flat or lightly dotted areas with 3-4 tones per material, so the piece looks thinner and flatter than the Beodeul houses with their per-tile tile and stone shading.
